_comment: TOM'S ALL-CLEARS, one per protected branch, pinned to the commit he cleared.
Keyed and pinned the way dev/english-key-rulings.json is keyed on the exact English text,
and for the same reason: AN APPROVAL MUST LAPSE BY ITSELF WHEN WHAT WAS APPROVED CHANGES.
Clear a branch at one commit, push three more, and 'head' no longer matches -- the gate
closes again without anybody remembering to close it.
WRITE HIS WORDS VERBATIM. 'Yes' and 'Yes, but drop the date validator' are both all-clears
and only one of them is finished. A boolean would lose the difference, which is exactly the
mistake the rulings file already avoids.
AI PROPOSES, TOM APPROVES, THEN AI WRITES -- never AI writing its own permission. If this
file is edited in the same session that merges the branch, and Tom's words are not in the
transcript, the gate has been walked around rather than passed.

674-coordinate-entry.words: I think this branch can be merged and deleted.
674-coordinate-entry.context: Said after he tested it, in the same message as his ruling that the Properties box does not need collapsing yet: "We discussed making Properties collapsible. To be honest, I don't think they are too long (long/numerous enough to need collapsing) yet."
674-coordinate-entry.pin_note: HE CLEARED IT AT bfd05abf AND THE PIN IS ONE COMMIT LATER, WHICH IS STATED RATHER THAN GLOSSED. The extra commit is 690a67c0, which applies HIS OWN three wording edits to lib/lang.ec.en.php -- lpn_coord_off_world, lpn_field_coord_tip and lpn_field_desc_tip -- harvested from the marks he wrote on dev/new-english-keys.md the same day. So the content of the commit he did not see is text he wrote himself. Recorded here because an all-clear is supposed to lapse when the branch moves, and this one was extended by a judgement rather than by him; if that judgement was wrong, the place to catch it is this line.

feat/library-import.head: 825d760e5cb8202f29e8c55a1f2e64eb2ce66225
feat/library-import.context: Cleared after his second round of testing. His three findings from the first round were all built before he cleared it: undo did not work (the document WAS being restored; the Libraries box was never rebuilt by undo, so it still listed rows that had gone), the wizard was not under File, and nothing said the incoming file's numbers were in different units. His own wording for the units warning was used verbatim, opening with 'Warning' and 'Not recommended', and the per-section buttons were removed so the File menu row is the only door -- which reversed an earlier instruction of his asking for both.

feat/customer-demands.head: 0476f882
feat/customer-demands.words: feat/customer-demands: Nice. Let's call it done, merge it, and delete it.
feat/customer-demands.context: Cleared in the same message as two other branch reports, after he had tested the branch on its preview port. THE COMMIT HE CLEARED IS THE OFFSET ONE and that is the point of the pin: Offset beside Station, in the properties box and in the customers table, was the thing he had asked for TWICE and had twice not been given -- 'I told you to add Offset in properties and tables. Do it.' He cleared the branch in the round after it finally landed. Nothing else was added between his test and this record.
feat/customer-demands.pin_note: PINNED TO THE SHORT SHA AS HE CLEARED IT. The branch was 8 commits BEHIND master when he cleared it, and master was deliberately NOT merged into the branch afterwards -- doing so would have moved the head and lapsed his approval for no gain, since the merge into master resolves the same divergence and is the tree the suite actually runs on.

feat/survey-import.head: f4ef6cdea957cd5353f6b285bd04a78b44e0e1f3
feat/survey-import.words: The task is complete. Merge, delete, and close.
feat/survey-import.context: Cleared after three rounds of his testing. His own wording throughout: the short PNEZD-only chooser, the cut format box, 'Create nodes' rather than 'Create junctions', 'specified internally' as text beside a disabled selector rather than inside the option, the asset-type selector first because a node's kind cannot be changed after import, and lower-case hyphenated error codes to match the CSV-validator world rather than the operating-system one. Units detection from a column name was REMOVED on his instruction -- a PNEZD file often has no header at all -- and GPX with it, since no seat had asked for it.

What he cleared is the map-attach wizard and the georeferencing work. WHAT HE HAS NOT CLEARED, AND MUST NOT BE READ AS CLEARED, IS TASK 703: he still sees white squares after four measured-and-fixed causes, and that task stays OPEN on master after this merge, as do queue rows R-019 and R-056.
feat/xy-world-map.pin_note: HE CLEARED IT AT 731ab367 AND THE PIN IS FOUR COMMITS LATER, WHICH IS STATED RATHER THAN GLOSSED, because those four are work he has not seen. They are: 5f2b49ab and 2b12b16d, the `?debug=tiles` readout -- an instrument built so HE can diagnose Task 703 himself, invisible to anyone who does not type the switch; 69d9c8ee, a fifth measured cause closed (a tile still hanging on screen under the new view was thrown away and re-fetched on an overshoot-and-correct gesture, with a harness and two killed mutations); and 5ade3041 and 765ac3bc, edits to dev/tom-review-queue.md, one of them deleting R-066 on his own written instruction (*"If it has been fixed, please delete this."*). The judgement made here was that an instrument switched off by default plus one measured defect fix is not a feature he needs to re-clear, and that leaving the branch alive for an open task is the stale-ref problem. If that judgement was wrong, this line is where to catch it.

feat/engine-fetch-wait.head: e9319a0ad8af40c6f86f2cee2204e80c95afbf96
feat/engine-fetch-wait.words: feat/engine-fetch-wait: Why is this branch still present? Is there something to do? Or merge, delete, and update?
feat/engine-fetch-wait.context: HIS WORDS ARE A QUESTION WITH TWO BRANCHES AND THE ANSWER TO THE FIRST IS NO, which is why this is recorded as an all-clear rather than glossed as one. He had already closed Task 608 outright on 2026-09-21 -- 'Done, right? Or is there more?' -- after testing the branch himself in a private window throttled to Slow 3G: 'Worked for me. No problems or alerts.' He also ruled all three halves on 2026-09-19: 'Continue working: Worked great. Banner can show always' and 'We must include the unknown in the progress bar. The progress bar can stall at the end if necessary. But it can't disappear prematurely.' Nothing was added to the branch after that ruling. dev/session-handoff.md said this branch had already MERGED and it had not, which is why he found it still on the preview panel.
feat/engine-fetch-wait.pin_note: PINNED TO THE BRANCH HEAD AS IT STANDS, e9319a0a, which is the commit he tested and ruled on. The merge into master resolved two conflicts, both of them bookkeeping and neither of them code: dev/ROADMAP.md, where master had already DELETED the closed Task 608 block and the branch still carried it (master's deletion kept), and dev/new-english-keys.md, which is a GENERATED file and was regenerated after the merge.

No shipped behaviour and no string moved. If extending the pin for a comment was the wrong call, this line is where to catch it.
